title: What If the Jet's Own Magnetic Field Had Weight?
hook: For fifty years the standard model of black hole jets treated their magnetic field as weightless. Let it gravitate and steady jets become impossible.
key_points: The Blandford-Znajek mechanism explains black hole jets as magnetic field lines extracting rotational energy.
It has always been a mechanism, not an exact solution: the field sits on a fixed spacetime and carries no mass of its own.
This paper instead lets a split-monopole field gravitate, giving a magnetic Reissner-Nordstrom geometry glued across an equatorial current sheet.
The author argues a truly steady jet is then impossible — a working jet is a black hole in decay.
Magnetic flux enters black hole mechanics as a charge, sharing one extremality budget with spin.
That budget caps jet power at c^5/48G regardless of the hole's mass, and limits lifetime output to about 9.2% of its mass.
content_html: The jets that shoot out of feeding black holes at nearly the speed of light are usually explained by the Blandford-Znajek mechanism: magnetic field lines threading the hole get twisted by its rotation and carry energy away. It has been the standard picture for fifty years, but it has always been a mechanism rather than an exact solution — the field is treated as a test field, riding on a spacetime it does not affect.
extra_html: In a new preprint, Yu Wang asks what changes when the jet's own field is allowed to gravitate. A split monopole field weighs the same as a magnetic monopole would, so its self-gravity produces the magnetic Reissner-Nordstrom geometry; gluing two copies across an equatorial current sheet puts the hole, its disk, and the jet-driving flux into a single spacetime, and adding force-free plasma makes a magnetosphere out of it. The author argues that three consequences follow that no test-field calculation could see. A steady jet becomes impossible: a slipping magnetosphere must heat the horizon, but a stationary horizon cannot be heated, so the only stationary configuration is a dead one corotating with the hole — a working jet is a black hole in decay. Magnetic flux enters the laws of black hole mechanics as a charge, sharing one extremality budget with spin, which caps jet power at c^5/48G whatever the mass. And the total lifetime output is finite, with a maximally spinning hole delivering about 9.2% of its mass. This is a single-author theoretical proposal rather than an observational result, and it will need scrutiny — but it is a rare attempt to make the jet's own weight part of the problem.

related.title: Physicists Recreated a Black Hole's Energy-Extraction Trick
related.hook: Roger Penrose showed a spinning black hole can hand energy to whatever passes through it. Physicists just reproduced that effect on a lab bench — no black hole, nothing spinning, required.

related.title: Stealing Energy From a Spin, No Event Horizon Required
related.hook: The Penrose process needs a black hole to swallow the negative-energy leftover. This paper argues a horizonless spinning object can trap it instead — and still hand you the profit.

related.title: Hawking's Black Hole Laws Get a Real-World Upgrade
related.hook: Hawking's famous black hole laws only strictly work for black holes frozen in perfect equilibrium. A new framework extends them to real black holes that merge, grow, and evaporate.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.

flashcards.prompt: What simplification does the standard Blandford-Znajek treatment of jets make?
flashcards.back_html: It solves force-free electrodynamics on a prescribed spacetime — the jet's own magnetic field is treated as a test field with no gravitational weight of its own.

flashcards.prompt: Why does letting the jet's magnetic flux gravitate cap the jet power?

choices.text: Flux then acts as a charge in black hole mechanics, sharing one extremality budget with spin
Because magnetic fields cannot exceed a fixed strength in vacuum
Because heavier black holes always produce weaker jets

flashcards.explanation_html: Treating flux as a charge means spin and flux draw on the same extremality limit, which the author argues bounds the power at c^5/48G independent of mass.

flashcards.prompt: Why does the author conclude a steady jet is impossible in this picture?
flashcards.back_html: A slipping magnetosphere necessarily heats the horizon, but a stationary horizon cannot be heated — so the only stationary state is a dead one corotating with the hole.
